audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal may escape both owner earnings and the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 finance-lease principal of $23.2 million; June 2026 finance-lease liability of $227.8 million, or $3.71 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If finance-lease depreciation is added back in OE without subtracting principal paid in financing cash flows, anchor OE is overstated; alternatively, the lease liability would require a bridge deduction, but not both.
audit_findings.evidence: For finance leases, the initial ROU asset is depreciated on a straight-line basis over the lease term, along with recognition of interest expense associated with accretion of the remaining lease liability, which is ultimately reduced by the related fixed payments as they are made.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting exposure is real, but the supplied record does not demonstrate that the OE calculation actually added back finance-lease depreciation without a compensating adjustment. If it did, the $23.2 million principal equals 2.5% of $910.2 million anchor OE. Even deducting the entire latest $227.8 million liability would reduce base value by only $3.71 per share, about 1.5% of the $14.730 billion base equity value. That scale would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2026 OE bridge, identify the $23.9 million finance-lease depreciation addback and $23.2 million principal treatment, and rerun OE only if principal was omitted; do not also deduct the liability if the recurring lease cost is retained in OE.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may normalize away a multi-year transformation program
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 NGT charges of $83.9 million, equal to 9.2% of anchor OE, plus $20.8 million in Q1 FY2027; exact valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Improperly excluding recurring NGT expenses raises anchor OE, while adding back amortization without including related recurring implementation investment understates maintenance capital.
audit_findings.evidence: The NGT project is expected to continue over the next several years, with implementation expected to occur in phases by region and/or capability, and involves the redesigning of certain end-to-end processes and the implementation of a suite of technology systems on a global scale.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not yet a demonstrated valuation error because the OE adjustment bridge and maintenance-capex schedule were not supplied. It is nevertheless materially open: the project began in FY2024, will continue for several years, and its FY2026 charges alone equal 9.2% of anchor OE, with another $20.8 million filed in the following quarter. If these costs were stripped from OE merely because management classified them outside segment profit, sustainable OE and all scenario values would be overstated.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2026 OE adjustment bridge and project-level cash schedule separating expensed charges, capital expenditures, capitalized cloud implementation costs, amortization, and genuinely nonrecurring items; rerun all scenarios with recurring NGT investment retained in OE or maintenance capital.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge assumes foreign cash is freely distributable and excess
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.593 billion of the latest $1.942 billion cash and short-term-investment balance was held abroad, or 82.0%; complete exclusion would equal $25.96 per share, but the appropriate haircut is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Taxes, legal restrictions, or operating-liquidity requirements reduce the cash amount that can be added to operating value in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of March 28, 2026, we had $2.065 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments, of which $1.403 billion were held by our subsidiaries domiciled outside the U.S.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that most cash is held abroad and that post-2017 foreign earnings are intended to be permanently reinvested, but it does not establish that this cash is trapped or quantify taxes and required operating balances. The potentially affected pool is large—complete exclusion would reduce the $240.08 base value by $25.96 per share, or 10.8%—so the issue cannot be dismissed, but the record cannot establish the actual material adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Map the June 2026 cash and short-term investments by entity and jurisdiction; quantify withholding, local, and U.S. taxes; identify restricted and minimum operating cash; then rerun the bridge using only surplus cash transferable to common shareholders.

audit_findings.title: An existing uncertain-tax claim is absent from the stated bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: June 2026 liability of $176.9 million, or $2.88 per share and 1.2% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any probability-weighted settlement not already reflected in normalized OE is a claim against cash and should reduce the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The total amount of unrecognized tax benefits, including interest and penalties, was $ 168.7 million and $ 193.3 million as of March 28, 2026 and March 29, 2025, respectively, and was included within the non-current liability for unrecognized tax benefits in the consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates an existing $176.9 million liability, but not that the full amount will be paid or that related cash taxes are absent from OE. Even deducting the entire liability—rather than a smaller probability-weighted amount—would reduce base value by only $2.88 per share, about 1.2% of the $14.730 billion base equity value, which is insufficient to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest uncertain-tax-position rollforward, audit status, expected settlement amounts and timing, and trace associated cash taxes through OE; deduct only the probability-weighted amount not already captured.
